 Most recent Most popular Post published at 16:10 GMT 16:10 GMT 
 It's all over in the 2pm matches, here are the results:
 Brighton 2-0 Brentford 
 Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool 
 Ipswich Town 1-2 Bournemouth 
 Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea 
 And here is how it leaves things in the Premier League table. Manchester United aiming to get out of the bottom three and Aston Villa bidding for a place in the top 10 before the international break.

 Villa's Old Trafford record not great published at 16:08 GMT 16:08 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Matthew Hobbs 
BBC Sport journalist 
 Since beating Manchester City in October, Villa have been knocked out of the League Cup at Bournemouth, drawn with Fulham and lost at the Nou Camp, so a rare away win in this fixture would be timely.
 Villa won their first Premier League match against United under Unai Emery in November 2022, but that came at home. Emery has never won in nine career attempts at Old Trafford, losing on all five visits with Villa.
 Now would be the perfect time to arrest that record as he approaches a 200th Premier League game as a manager.
 The 55-year-old will become the fifth Spaniard to reach the milestone after Rafael Benitez, Roberto Martinez, Pep Guardiola, and Mikel Arteta.
 Benitez and Arteta's 200th matches also came against United, and both avoided defeats.
 8 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Greatest club in the world' published at 16:06 GMT 16:06 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Chief Football News Reporter at Old Trafford 
 We've just had the first reading of the teams from the stadium announcer.
 He finished off by saying 'let's get behind the reds' and called Manchester United 'the greatest club in the world'.
 I know there is a PR element to that and it is his job to create positivity but I saw Crystal Palace concede a third goal and my first thought was 'Manchester United can't be bottom during the international break'.
 That is just mad.
 11 29 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Emery deserves everything at Villa' published at 16:03 GMT 16:03 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Tommy Smith 
Former Middlesbrough Town defender on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 People are saying they would love to see Unai Emery at Manchester United but at Aston Villa he has got total control and would he get that at United? There is an argument to say no he wouldn't.
 Emery deserves everything he gets at Villa - a new contract is a smack in the face to other clubs to say 'this is our manager' and he deserves it. What he has done consistently over the last few years is transition a playing squad to get the absolute maximum out of those players.
 The players that have left the club in the last few years - Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Emi Martinez - significant players that have left and he continues to churn out results and performances.
 31 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 200 up for Emery published at 16:00 GMT 16:00 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 This will be Aston Villa boss Unai Emery’s 200th Premier League game in charge. He’s the fifth Spaniard to reach this milestone after Rafael Benítez, Roberto Martínez, Pep Guardiola, and Mikel Arteta, with Benítez’s (2-0 win) and Arteta’s (1-1 draw) 200th games also coming against Man Utd.
 And what a job he has done.
 Image source, Getty Images

 Emery to United? Doesn't look like it published at 15:57 GMT 15:57 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Football is funny sometimes, isn't it.
 Manchester United are in a dire situation and, to get themselves out of trouble, must beat Unai Emery's Aston Villa. A side who also had a poor start to the season but seem to be turning things around under one of the most respected coaches in the game.
 A coach that many United fans would like to see in their own dugout and who has been heavily linked with the job, should United choose to part ways with Michael Carrick.
 It looks like that won't happen given what Guillem Balague has just said.
 But it feels like the two clubs are heading in complete opposite directions.
 33 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Emery close to new Villa deal published at 15:54 GMT 15:54 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Guillem Balague 
Spanish football journalist 
 Aston Villa head coach Unai Emery is close to agreeing a contract extension at the club - which will hand him even more responsibility for long-term development.
 The Villa boss held talks with the hierarchy on Wednesday to discuss the club's future, with all parties keen on extending his time at Villa Park.
 Emery would relish the opportunity to play an even bigger role in developing the club for the long term, with talks ongoing about the fine details, the finances, and the length of the new deal.
 The plan is to announce the new contract once all details have been agreed.

 No international break plans for Carrick published at 15:51 GMT 15:51 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Chief Football News Reporter at Old Trafford 
 Manchester United's hierarchy are expected to assess the situation at the club during the forthcoming international break.
 They committed to giving Michael Carrick and his players a chance to turn the situation around after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth a fortnight ago, since when they performed well in the first-half against Chelsea, but lost, and badly in the first half against Roma but won, thrillingly, in the Champions League.
 For all the debate about Carrick's future, he has no special plans for the couple of weeks between today and the trip to Liverpool.
 "We're just carrying on as normal," said Carrick.
 "International breaks are
always a time, when talking about the players that aren't going away
and for the staff, to re-energise and freshen up.
 "There is an element of that, but I don't
really need it. I'm fine as I am." 
 24 12 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 15:48 GMT 15:48 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 It's difficult to unpick the amount of noise, opinion and issues surrounding Manchester United at the moment.
 From players speaking out against the manager and hierarchy, to attempts to paper over cracks with talk of a new stadium, a 'will they, won't they' saga around whether Michael Carrick will get the sack, fan protests and, probably worst of all, a terrible run of form on the pitch which now sees them inside the Premier League relegation zone.
 The buck often stops with the manager. But when United have tried the 'hiring and firing' game and it hasn't worked - where do they go from here?

 Man Utd boss has to perform with hands tied published at 15:45 GMT 15:45 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Paul Robinson 
Former Leeds goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 The response Michael Carrick got from those supporters [after the 3-0 loss against Bournemouth].
 Football supporters nowadays are very educated and they understand. 
 The vehicles that they have with social media, the channels they can get their information from. Football supporters are more educated than they have been in a long time. 
 Those fans know if it is not Carrick, then whoever is standing in that dugout is performing with their hands tied behind their back.

 'Time for Carrick to take ownership' published at 15:40 GMT 15:40 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Julien Laurens 
French football journalist on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 If there is another first half like the one in the Champions League against Roma, Manchester United might not come back from that this time. 
 It's time for Michael Carrick to take some ownership. He has to take responsibility for choices that he has made - like dropping Bruno Fernandes.
 He has to take ownership if he wants to get out of this crisis and this is a crisis - they are deep in crisis.

 Post published at 15:37 GMT 15:37 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Just how crucial could that comeback win over Roma in the Champions League be for Manchester United and for Michael Carrick's job?
 If United rediscover the level they managed to find against the Serie A side in the second half earlier this week and get a win this afternoon...It could prove to be a massive turning point.
 Matheus Cunha scored two goals and was massively fired up, so much so that he was sent off for a second yellow card for excessive celebration.
 If United can find some of that intensity and desire, will things improve?

 Can Man Utd ride Roma wave? published at 15:34 GMT 15:34 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Matthew Hobbs 
BBC Sport journalist 
 Manchester United's comeback win against Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday provided some welcome respite for beleaguered manager Michael Carrick, along with some welcome fight from his players.
 United responded to going two goals down in the opening 18 minutes by producing arguably their finest 45 minutes of the campaign so far in the second half, with forward Matheus Cunha capping off a 3-2 victory.
 For the first time this season, they prevented their opponent from having a shot in the second half and won more duels (41) than in any other game after half-time.
 The challenge for Carrick and his players alike will be to repeat that performance across 90 minutes five days later in the Premier League.
 United are one of only two sides without a Premier League clean sheet this season, along with Ipswich Town, while nine matches is the longest period they have gone from the start of a top-flight campaign without recording a shutout since 1987.
 The last side to finish in the top three of the top flight then fail to keep a clean sheet in their first 10 games of the following season was Liverpool 50 years ago.
 Carrick's side have not won in the Premier League since beating Ipswich on 30 August – this match takes place 70 days, or 1,680 hours, after that solitary victory.
 19 16 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Still feel United are not far from another collapse' published at 15:32 GMT 15:32 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Image source, BBC Sport There were great scenes at Old Trafford on Tuesday with Manchester United coming back from 2-0 down to beat Roma , who had to field their third-choice goalkeeper because of injuries.
 That ended up being a really good result, but there are so many things about United that are just not convincing at the moment - as a club they are trying to convey this picture of togetherness and it is just not there for me.
 Beating Roma was a great comeback, of course, but you still feel United are not far from another collapse, especially against an Aston Villa team who are so well structured, and capable of punishing any weakness.
 Villa boss Unai Emery has been talked about as a potential successor to Michael Carrick at Old Trafford, but he is too good for United as far as I can see.
 United will score, but Villa are going to win this. Nicolas Jackson will bag a couple and we might see more tears from Bruno Fernandes at the final whistle.
 Sutton's prediction: 1-3

 Team news - Tielemans starts, Lacey on bench; Garnacho not involved for Villa published at 15:29 GMT 15:29 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Chief Football News Reporter at Old Trafford 
 Youri Tielemans replaces injured midfielder Carlos Baleba
and Noussair Mazraoui is recalled for Ayden Heaven as Michael Carrick makes two
changes to the side that beat Roma on Tuesday.
 Amad Diallo retains his spot, so Shea Lacey must wait to
make his first Premier League start. Lisandro Martinez is ruled out following
his controversial dismissal at Chelsea.
 Man Utd XI: Lammens, Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Mazraoui, Tielemans,
Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes, Cunha, Mbeumo. 
 Subs: Darlow, De
Ligt, Mount, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Andrey Santos, Heaven, Lacey, J Fletcher.
 Unai Emery makes three changes to the side hammered in Barcelona,
with former Manchester United defender Victor Lindelof set to start at right-back. 
 There is no place in the Villa squad for Alejandro Garnacho, who has struggled
to make an impact since leaving Old Trafford in the summer of 2025. Taylor
Harwood-Bellis, Allyson and Leon Goretkza are all recalled. 
 Aston Villa XI: 
Suzuki, Lindelof, Harwood-Bellis, Torres, Maatsen, Alysson, Kamara, McGinn,
Goretzka, Manzambi, Jackson. 
 Subs: Bizot, Mings, Barkley, Buendia, Mbaye,
Gomes, Madjo, Cisse, Hemmings.

 'You don't know what you're going to get from Man Utd' published at 15:27 GMT 15:27 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Paul Robinson 
Former Leeds goalkeeper on BBC Radio 5 Live 
 Aston Villa have not won in their last three. They're going to be going there looking for a result. 
 With Manchester United it is difficult because you don't know what you're going to get from them. Michael Carrick unearthed something at half-time against Roma. 
 He found a spirit, no matter who you play for, no matter what club you play for, all the clubs I have played for the minimum requirement is maximum effort. He hasn't always got that from his team. 
 So many times we talk about them being outrun, outfought, their physical stats against other teams weren't at a level that they should be. 
 That half-time team talk found something and the way Manchester United came out in the second half against Roma, they have to do that again this weekend. 
 42 8 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Four minutes to forget published at 15:24 GMT 15:24 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 For a spell of about four minutes in the first halves of the 2pm matches, Manchester United were BOTTOM of the Premier League. Incredible, really.
 Liverpool currently lead Crystal Palace 2-0 and that looks like it will condemn them to bottom place. Regardless, United are firmly in the relegation zone and need a win today otherwise they will be stranded there over the international break.
 Own up to it, who was screenshotting the Premier League table to taunt their United-supporting friends/colleagues?
 43 23 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Man Utd bid to avoid international break embarrassment published at 15:21 GMT 15:21 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 Simon Stone 
BBC Sport Chief Football News Reporter at Old Trafford 
 Nottingham Forest's shock triumph over Manchester City last night dumped Manchester United into the relegation zone.
 It is not somewhere they have been after a match round since 1986-87, when Sir Alex Ferguson's second match as manager ended in a 0-0 draw at Norwich.
 If United don't beat Aston Villa today, they will remain in the bottom three throughout the international window, knowing their next game is at old rivals Liverpool on 22 November.
 As Michael Carrick points out in his programme notes, his side can't allow Thursday's thrilling victory over Roma to be a one-off.
 "While we can be really pleased with elements of the performance
on Tuesday night, we must absolutely know there is so much more to come from
our team," he outlines. 
 "We must be ready to show that we can back up Tuesday’s
victory and begin to create the momentum to give ourselves something to build
on after the international break."
 24 14 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Man Utd must win to get out of drop zone published at 15:18 GMT 15:18 GMT 
 Man Utd v Aston Villa (16:30 GMT) 
 So, here we go.
 Anything other than a win and Manchester United will enter the international break in the bottom three of the Premier League.
 They have registered just one top-flight win this season. Will Michael Carrick be sacked if they don't win today? Who would they even bring in? Just what is going on at Manchester United at the moment?
 By contrast, although Aston Villa lost in the Champions League to a brilliant Barcelona side in midweek, they are starting to find their feet in the league.
 It could be a tough old day for United and their fans.
